rootCauses.title: body's overflow value is not propagated to the viewport: a body with a definite height and overflow:hidden|auto|scroll becomes its own scroll container, so the viewport has no scrollable overflow
rootCauses.area: vendor/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs (flush_styles_to_layout_impl), vendor/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs (scroll_state, canonical_scroll_target), vendor/blitz-paint/src/render.rs (should_clip), vendor/blitz-dom/src/node/scrollbar.rs, crates/script/src/layout.rs (n_scroll_metrics/n_set_scroll for body)
rootCauses.mechanism: CSS Overflow 3 §3.3: when the root element is <html> with overflow:visible in both axes and it has a <body> child, the body's overflow-* values are applied to the viewport instead and the body's USED overflow becomes visible (visible->auto, clip->hidden on the viewport). CSSOM View: documentElement.scrollHeight (standards mode) = max(viewport scrolling-area height, viewport height). Sharko implements propagation only for the root element itself (scrolling.rs:30-32 and :272-283 map ScrollTarget::Node(root) to Viewport; render.rs:406-409 never clips the root) but never for body. The body's taffy style is built verbatim from stylo computed values in flush_styles_to_layout_impl (vendor/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:576-586 via stylo_taffy::to_taffy_style -> convert.rs:268-275: hidden->Hidden, auto/scroll->Scroll), so body is a taffy scroll container (taffy/src/style/mod.rs:391-396 is_scroll_container). Consequences: (1) in taffy's block/flex/grid layout the children's overflow of a scroll-container child is not added to the parent's scrollable_overflow_rect (block.rs compute_scrollable_overflow_contribution uses item.overflow), so <html>'s Layout.scrollable_overflow_rect.bottom stays at html's own height (800px when html{height:100%} or body{height:100vh}); (2) crates/script/src/layout.rs:71-83 document_scroll_size and vendor/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:444-471 viewport scroll_state both read html's size/scrollable_overflow_rect -> documentElement.scrollHeight = 800 and viewport max scroll = 0 (window.scrollTo is a no-op, window.scrollY stays 0, no 'scroll' events on window/document); (3) scrolling.rs:473-505 treats body as a scroll target with range = its content, so wheel, scrollIntoView and focus scrolling move body.scrollTop instead of the viewport (wetter.com: body.scrollTop = 9405 = body.scrollHeight - 800 after the CMP container got focused, so the screenshot shows the footer and the consent dialog is pushed below the viewport); (4) vendor/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:381-415 should_clip reads stylo overflow_x/y and clips body's content to 800px and node/scrollbar.rs:77-100 draws scrollbars on body; (5) headless CaptureFullPage (crates/browser/src/headless.rs:495-499) sizes the frame from the document scroll height -> a 1280x800 'full page' screenshot. Chromium propagates: documentElement.scrollHeight = content height, viewport scrolls (hidden -> not user-scrollable but programmatically scrollable), body.scrollTop stays 0.
evidence: r9 (html{height:100%} body{height:100%;overflow:auto;display:flex} + 5000px child) -> Chromium: documentElement.scrollHeight 5000, window.scrollTo(0,1e5) -> scrollY 4200; Sharko: 800, scrollTo -> 0, body.scrollHeight 5000

r8 (same with body overflow:hidden = scroll lock) -> Chromium 5000 / scrollTo 4200; Sharko 800 / 0. r11 (bsky pattern: html{min-height:100%;display:flex} body{height:100vh;overflow-y:scroll;display:flex}) -> Chromium 5000 / 4200; Sharko 800 / 0
Sharko `--scroll=1000` on r9 -> window.scrollY 0, document.body.scrollTop 1000, documentElement.scrollTop 0: the user's wheel scrolls the body element, not the viewport (no window scroll events)
Sharko `--screenshot --full-page` on r9 -> PNG 1280x800 (control r5 with plain tall body -> 1280x5000): the full-page capture is truncated to the viewport
zdf.de live: Chromium documentElement.scrollHeight 7671 (body relative/hidden/flex h=800, html h=800, scrollTo -> 6871); Sharko 800 (body.scrollHeight 7671, scrollTo -> 0)
pinterest.de live: Chromium 5536 (body relative + inline `overflow:hidden`, h=800, scrollTo 4736); Sharko 800 (body.scrollHeight 4166, scrollTo 0)
bsky.app live: Chromium 6086 (html{min-height:100%;display:flex}, body{overflow-y:scroll;display:flex;h=800}, scrollTo 5286); Sharko 800 (body.scrollHeight 26056, scrollTo 0)

wetter.com live in Sharko (CMP open: body.cmp-prevent-scroll -> overflow hidden, h=800, html min-height 100%): documentElement.scrollHeight 800, body.scrollHeight 10205, body.scrollTop 9405, activeElement = DIV#cmp-wetter; sweep screenshot shows the page footer instead of the top + dialog. Chromium sweep: 10178

Code: vendor/blitz-dom/src has no body->viewport propagation (grep propagat: only the root-element comments in scrolling.rs:30,273); render.rs:406-409 exempts only the root from clipping; scrolling.rs:480-493 decides scrollability from stylo overflow of the node itself

WPT: `node tools/wpt/run.js --filter="scrollHeight|scrollWidth|scrolling-area|overflow" css/cssom-view` -> 12 tests, 456/539 subtests, no change vs tools/wpt/expected.json; none of the testharness tests there gives body a definite height + non-visible overflow, and the css/css-overflow propagation reftests are absent from the checkout / skipped by the runner (run.js:143 testharness only), so this gap is invisible to WPT

repro.expected: Chromium: documentElement.scrollHeight 5000, clientHeight 800, window.scrollTo(0,100000) -> scrollY 4200, body.scrollTop 0, wheel scrolls the viewport, full-page screenshot 5000px tall
repro.actual: Sharko: documentElement.scrollHeight 800, scrollTo -> scrollY 0, body.scrollHeight 5000, wheel scrolls body.scrollTop (window.scrollY stays 0), body clips at 800px, --full-page screenshot 1280x800

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high — `html,body{height:100%}` + `body{overflow:auto|hidden}` and `body{height:100vh; overflow-y:scroll}` are standard app-shell patterns (React Native Web/bsky, Next.js sites like zdf), and virtually every CMP/modal scroll lock sets body overflow:hidden; on such pages window.scrollY/scrollHeight/scroll events are wrong and lazy-load / infinite-scroll code keyed on window scrolling never fires
rootCauses.fixSketch: Implement CSS Overflow 3 §3.3 in blitz-dom: (1) in flush_styles_to_layout_impl (damage.rs:576-631) or a tiny pre-pass in resolve_layout, decide the viewport overflow source: root element if its stylo overflow_x/y are not both Visible, else the first <body> element child of an <html> root; store doc.viewport_overflow: Point<Overflow> (visible->Auto, clip->Hidden) and set a NodeFlags::OVERFLOW_PROPAGATED_TO_VIEWPORT on the source node; for that node force taffy_style.overflow = Point{Visible,Visible} (its used value) so taffy's block/flex/grid overflow contribution flows into <html>.scrollable_overflow_rect and document_scroll_size (crates/script/src/layout.rs:71) and viewport scroll_state (scrolling.rs:444) become correct without further changes. Re-evaluate the flag whenever root/body overflow changes (CMPs toggle it): mark root+body LAYOUT_DIRTY when the source or value changes. (2) scrolling.rs: canonical_scroll_target (:274) maps a flagged node to ScrollTarget::Viewport (like the root), so wheel chaining (events/pointer.rs:828 handle_wheel -> scroll_chain_by), scrollIntoView, focus scrolling and body.scrollTop writes go to the viewport; viewport scroll_state (:444-471) returns a zero range per axis for user scrolls when doc.viewport_overflow is Hidden (include_hidden=false) — this also fixes the inverse bug that html{overflow:hidden} currently lets the user wheel-scroll (r12: Sharko scrollY 1000, Chromium blocks user scroll but allows scrollTo). (3) blitz-paint render.rs:409: `!is_root_element && !flagged` before clipping; node/scrollbar.rs:77-100: no scrollbars on the flagged node; the engine's viewport scrollbar should follow doc.viewport_overflow (Scroll -> always, Auto -> when overflowing, Hidden -> never). (4) crates/script/src/layout.rs n_scroll_metrics/n_set_scroll: for the flagged body return scrollTop/Left 0 and ignore writes per CSSOM View (body is not the scrollingElement in standards mode; quirks mode is a separate follow-up, see expected.json FAILs in scrolling-quirks-vs-nonquirks.html). (5) Regression tests: r8/r9/r11 as engine tests (documentElement.scrollHeight, window.scrollTo, body.scrollTop==0, wheel -> window.scrollY); enable css/css-overflow overflow-body-propagation reftests once the WPT runner handles reftests.

rootCauses.title: heise.de/spiegel.de (and faz.net at sweep time): the 800-vs-34216 gap is a state mismatch — Sourcepoint's scroll lock (body position:fixed; overflow:hidden) was active in Sharko but the CMP never appeared in the Chromium sweep run; with the lock active Chromium also reports 800
rootCauses.area: tools/sitediff/probe.js / tools/sitediff/run.js (record overlay/lock state or dismiss CMPs before measuring); no engine change
rootCauses.mechanism: Sourcepoint adds html.sp-message-open and styles body {position:fixed; overflow:hidden} while its consent dialog (#sp_message_container_*, position:fixed, z-index 2147483647) is open. A fixed-positioned box is out of flow and does not contribute to the viewport's scrollable overflow (CSS Overflow 3 §2.2 counts boxes for which the scroll container is the containing block; the fixed body's containing block is the viewport, and it does not scroll with it), so the viewport scrolling area is just the <html> box (800px with html{height:100%}). Chromium behaves exactly like this (repros r1/r2/r7 and the live sites today). Sharko matches on purpose: vendor/taffy/src/compute/block.rs:1930-1941 (PATCH from commit bdb05d1) excludes position:fixed children from the container's scrollable overflow, and vendor/blitz-dom/src/layout/abspos.rs re-positions fixed boxes against the viewport without touching the root's overflow rect. The sweep's Chromium numbers (34216 / 33701 / 30567) were measured on an unlocked page: tools/sitediff/out/heise.de/chromium.json contains no sp_message_container and zero position:fixed elements in its element sample, while sharko.json lists #sp_message_container_1511493 (fixed, 1280x800). The CMP's appearance is timing/network dependent (Chromium's heise load took 24 s through the proxy), so the two runs measured different states.
evidence: r1 (body{position:fixed;overflow:hidden;width:100%} + 5000px child) -> Chromium: documentElement.scrollHeight 800, html height 0px, scrollTo -> 0; Sharko: identical (800 / 0px / 0). r2 (fixed div with 5000px child) -> 800 in both; r7 (fixed body, overflow visible) -> 800 in both; r3 (absolute div) -> 5000 in both

heise.de live today: Chromium documentElement.scrollHeight 800, clientHeight 800, html.sp-message-open, body position fixed / overflow hidden / h=32624, scrollTo -> 0; Sharko: 800 / same state / body h=32984 / scrollTo -> 0
spiegel.de live today: Chromium 800 (sp-message-open, body fixed/hidden h=31085); Sharko 800 (same state, body h=31434)

Sweep artefacts: heise chromium.json has 0 elements with position fixed and 0 occurrences of 'sp_message'; sharko.json lists #sp_message_container_1511493 (fixed, [0,0,1280,800]) and a-sticky-footer (fixed) -> the Chromium sweep measured the page without the consent dialog and its scroll lock

faz.net today (no Sourcepoint lock in either browser): Chromium 30567 vs Sharko 23116 with body static — the sweep's 800 for faz was the lock state (sharko.json mentions sp_message), the remaining gap is a layout-height difference belonging to another cluster

repro.expected: Chromium: documentElement.scrollHeight 800 (viewport), body.scrollHeight 5050, window cannot scroll (scrollTo -> 0)
repro.actual: Sharko: identical (800 / 5050 / 0) — no engine bug; the sweep compared a locked Sharko page with an unlocked Chromium page

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: low — engine-wise none (Sharko is spec-correct and matches Chromium); for the sweep, every Sourcepoint/OneTrust site is exposed to this false positive unless the CMP state is equalised
rootCauses.fixSketch: In tools/sitediff/probe.js record the scroll-lock state (body/html computed position + overflow-y, classes such as sp-message-open, and any position:fixed element covering >=90% of the viewport with its z-index) and have run.js/clusters treat 'documentElement.scrollHeight == viewport' as expected when body is position:fixed in that engine; better, dismiss consent dialogs in both engines before measuring (Sharko has --click-text; Playwright can click the same text) or wait until both engines agree on the presence of the overlay. Optionally also compare body.scrollHeight, which is 32984 vs 32624 here and shows the content is laid out.

notes: o2online.de: not a scroll-size problem — Sharko rendered only 542 elements (Chromium 2675), body/html height 436px with a Usercentrics dialog and 310 console errors; the app content never rendered (JS/app-init failure, other cluster). svelte.dev: Sharko shows the site's own '500' error page (skipped as instructed). faz.net today: 23116 (Sharko) vs 30567 (Chromium) with no lock in either browser — a layout-height difference, not this mechanism. bsky.app: besides the propagation bug, body.scrollHeight is 26056 in Sharko vs 6086 in Chromium (feed items laid out much taller) — separate layout issue. wetter.com: the fixed CMP container ended up focused and Sharko scrolled *body* to its static position at the end of the content (body.scrollTop 9405), which is why the sweep screenshot shows the footer and no dialog; this is a consequence of root cause 1 (body wrongly being a scroll container), the same fix removes it. Inverse bug found on the way (r12): html{overflow:hidden} does not prevent user wheel scrolling in Sharko (scrollY 1000 after --scroll=1000; Chromium keeps the user at 0 while scrollTo still works) — scrolling.rs viewport scroll_state ignores the propagated overflow value; covered by step (2) of the fix sketch. Environment: both engines went through the same proxy; the CMP appearance is nondeterministic across runs (heise/spiegel/faz/wetter differed between the sweep and today's probes in both browsers), so page-height comparisons need the overlay state recorded. WPT: the css/cssom-view scroll-size filter shows no change against expected.json; the checkout has no css/css-overflow propagation tests (only scroll-markers) and the runner skips reftests, so root cause 1 is not caught by the current WPT setup — add the r8/r9/r11 repros as engine regression tests. Quirks-mode body scrolling (HTMLBody-ScrollArea_quirksmode.html, scrolling-quirks-vs-nonquirks.html FAILs in expected.json) is a related but separate follow-up.
